answer: Earning one unit of timber for trade execution requires solving sequential client tasks hash-linked along a vine so each step awaits the prior graded output. Juries test error correlation across submissions; when accounts share failure modes from one policy, the $j$-th linked account must extend its vine by $j$ judged tasks and burn $30j$ copper in jury fees. A solo entrant solves 1 task and burns 30 copper per timber, whereas an operator running $m$ clones from one policy must complete $m(m+1)/2$ sequential tasks and burn $15m(m+1)$ copper, or train $m$ uncorrelated policies.
